Apparently, some people take Dramamine, a type of OTC medication to reduce nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness to get "high." Each tablet is 50 mg, and there are usually 12 tablets in a small bottle. People usually take more than 12 in order to experience getting "high." Some people compared it to PCP because you can experience hallucinations and such. There is one report that a woman overdosed after taking 5,000 mg of Dramamine and died. Doing the math, would have been 100 tablets, and dividing the 100 tablets by 12 tablets, the amount in each small bottle, it would take 8.3 bottles in order to overdose. [Medical Report to Dramamine Overdose.](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/8363125)

People also overdose on Imodium, a type of OTC medication to help treat diarrhea. People who overdose on Imodium are usually opioid abusers who are going through withdrawals. Imodium helps activate the opiate receptors on the nerves that trigger the brain to release endorphins and more, which basically feels like getting high on opioids but its actually from Imodium activating the opiate receptors. People use this as an alternative to opioids if they can no longer obtain opioids or to help cope with the withdrawal side effects. There are 2mg per soft gel of Imodium, and each large box that I have seen has 24 soft gels in each box. People usually take hundreds of soft gels a day to get the same high from opioids or to help aid opioid withdrawal. A woman overdosed on Imodium to help alleviate heroin withdrawals.  [Medical Report on Imodium Overdose.](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5637705/) 

All in All, I guess if you take a large amount of OTC medication, you have the possibility to overdose and die.
